ask_fleet, ask_body, ask_goals, ask_pantry and ask_mail ran SubAgent.investigate before Live could speak: up to four sequential Flash-Lite POSTs, one to pick tools and another to compose prose that Live then rephrased anyway. They now call SubAgent.route, which makes one POST with the domain's tools, runs whatever the model picked in parallel under each tool's own timeout, and hands the raw results back framed as "Results for <question>. SubAgent gains an internal transport seam so SubAgentRouteTest drives it with a fake: one POST with tools picked, the no-tool text path, failure mapping, per-tool and whole-route timeouts. Books convert: pin PyMuPDF 1.28.2 and ebooklib 0.20, the ticket's fallback over Calibre
books 04
077bfc6e · 1 file
The image change for books ticket 04, on its own as the ticket asks. No Dockerfile text changes: both install from wheels in the existing `pip install -r requirements.txt` layer, so no apt package is added. Why not Calibre, the ticket's primary. Traced from Debian's trixie Packages index (python:3.13-slim is trixie, per docker-library's tag list): `calibre` 8.5.0+ds-1+deb13u3 with --no-install-recommends pulls 370 packages, 1105 MB installed on amd64 and 1064 MB on arm64, on top of what the image already carries (curl and postgresql-client-17 are 75 MB). The image is roughly 400 MB today, so Calibre lands it at the ~1.5 GB line the ticket names. Its largest pieces are Chromium (libqt6webenginecore6, 182 MB), LLVM 19 for Mesa, SciPy, and Debian's own python3.13 beside the image's /usr/local one. And with no Docker on this machine it could not be run headless anywhere before production. The ticket names this fallback for exactly those cases. PyMuPDF 1.28.2 (2026-08-06) rather than 2.0 (2026-10-19): four days old, and 2.0 declares numpy, onnxruntime and networkx as hard dependencies. 1.28.2 has none and ships abi3 manylinux_2_28 wheels for x86_64 and aarch64, so Cloud Run and the Oracle A1 image both install it without a compiler. lxml 6.1.3 is ebooklib's, pinned with the transitive block; six was already pinned. PyMuPDF and ebooklib are AGPL-3.0; the service's source is this public repository. Unverified until deploy: the image build itself (no Docker here). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ca83deed · 48 files
event-sheet.tsx is one form for both surfaces: a bottom sheet at family width and a right-hand panel at workbench width, mounted once in the signed-in shell so the "+" on Home, a row and (next) the calendar all open the same thing. Title, all day, date, start and end, Repeats (never, daily, weekly with weekday chips, monthly, yearly; ends never / on a date / after N), reminder from the engine's allowed set, location, notes, and Shared / Only me (default Shared). Not optimistic. A refusal stays in the sheet, the engine's sentence verbatim under "Nothing was saved." Saving or deleting one occurrence of a series asks "Just this one" or "All of them" before any write: just-this-one skips the date and, on an edit, POSTs a one-off keyed "<series id>:<YYYY-MM-DD>"; all-of-them PATCHes or DELETEs the series, shifting the series start by however far the date moved and carrying an "every 2 weeks" the form has no control for. If the one-off fails after the skip, the sentence says the occurrence IS out of the series; Save again finishes it (skip is idempotent, create is keyed). A Canvas row is not offered for editing: the poller rewrites it every half hour. Pure form rules live in lib/event-form.ts with their own tests.
